name: Zhang Yanbo
current_role: Co-founder, Linkerbot (灵心巧手, Beijing) - leads external product and industry communication
profile: Zhang Yanbo (张延柏, also romanised Zhang Yanbai) is co-founder of Linkerbot, a Beijing robotics company founded in 2023 that makes the Linker Hand series of dexterous robotic hands for humanoid and embodied-AI robots. Backed by Sequoia China (HongShan) among others, it was valued around $3B per Hurun; customers reportedly include BYD, Midea, Samsung and Siemens.
interesting_fact: Linkerbot claims over 80% of the global market for high-degree-of-freedom dexterous hands; its Linker Hand O6 sells for 6,666 yuan, weighs 370 g and can carry up to 50 kg, and it targets 50,000-100,000 units a year in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He calls the dexterous hand the 'last centimeter' (最后一厘米) of embodied AI - the deciding factor in a robot's manipulation ability; the company's 21-DoF Linker Hand L20 with tactile 'electronic skin' showed off by threading a needle in a February 2026 Beijing demo.
notes: Little personal biography is public; most coverage is Chinese-language (BJNews, NBD, 36Kr). Founder/CEO Zhou Yong (Alex Zhou) is the company's main spokesperson.

name: Mark Rosenzweig
current_role: Founder of SharkNinja (Shark and Ninja brands); no current executive or board role found
profile: Montreal-born entrepreneur who in 1994 founded Euro-Pro Operating, a housewares firm making steam cleaners and vacuums, launched the Shark brand in 2007 and Ninja kitchen appliances in 2009; the company was renamed SharkNinja in 2015 and is now NYSE-listed. CEO Mark Barrocas runs the company; SharkNinja still credits Rosenzweig as founder.
interesting_fact: Shark's 'No-Loss-of-Suction' vacuums let the then-small Euro-Pro overtake Dyson in the US upright-vacuum market - Forbes ran the 2014 story 'How Shark Ate Dyson's Lunch In America'.
deep_cut_fact: Euro-Pro grew out of a Rosenzweig family housewares business that had run for generations in Montreal; he moved the company's headquarters from Montreal to Needham, Massachusetts in 2003, where SharkNinja is still based.
notes: Identity flag: the input lists 'Ninja (founder; company valued $2B)' from Hurun's unicorn list, but SharkNinja is a public company worth far more and founded in 1994 (Hurun's unicorn index covers private firms founded after 2000). Saudi q-commerce unicorn 'Ninja' was founded by Saud Al Qahtani and Canberk Donmez, not him. Could be a Hurun data mismatch. Very private; no personal social accounts found.
